message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(n=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work modulo \(p\).

We use the congruence
\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv (-4)^k\binom{n}{k}\pmod p,\qquad 0\le k<p.
\]
For \(k>n\), this is \(0\equiv 0\) modulo \(p\) because \(p\le 2k<2p\), so \(p\mid \binom{2k}{k}\). For \(0\le k\le n\),
\[
(-4)^k\binom{n}{k}
=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{-4(n-j)}{j+1}
\equiv \prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{2(2j+1)}{j+1}
=\binom{2k}{k}.
\]

Thus
\[
S\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{p-1} k\binom{n}{k}(-8)^k
=\sum_{k=0}^{n} k\binom{n}{k}(-8)^k.
\]
By differentiating \((1+y)^n\),
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{n} k\binom{n}{k}y^k=ny(1+y)^{n-1}.
\]
With \(y=-8\),
\[
S\equiv -8n(-7)^{n-1}.
\]

Now observe
\[
2027=2^2+7\cdot 17^2.
\]
Modulo \(2027\), this gives \(7\cdot 17^2\equiv -4\), so
\[
-7\equiv \left(2\cdot 17^{-1}\right)^2.
\]
Hence \(-7\) is a quadratic residue modulo \(2027\), so
\[
(-7)^n\equiv 1 \pmod{2027}.
\]
Therefore
\[
(-7)^{n-1}\equiv (-7)^{-1},
\]
and
\[
S\equiv -8n(-7)^{-1}=\frac{8n}{7}.
\]
Since \(8n=4(p-1)\equiv -4\pmod p\),
\[
S\equiv -4\cdot 7^{-1}.
\]
But \(7\cdot 17^2=2023\equiv -4\pmod{2027}\), so
\[
S\equiv 17^2=289.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
